title: Billing Department Rule: Program Charges Billed on Electric Service by Rate Schedule Accounts
content:
**When a program charge is billed.** A program charge is billed on the Electric Service by Rate Schedule bill only when another cooperative program's own record produces it:

| Producing program | Program charge |
|---|---|
| Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements) | The arrangement's monthly installment, or its billed-back balance |
| PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) | Unrecovered PrePay Power arrears |
| Area and Security Lighting Rental | An area light rental, or an area light charge |

Budget Billing never produces a program charge, because the actual charges already stand on the account and a settle-up only changes the amount due.

**Amount and reference.** The amount of a program charge is taken verbatim from that program record, and its source is that record.

**Past-due and late charge treatment — no longer in force.** The former clause stating that program charges count toward the past-due amount and the late charge like any other charge is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current late payment charge basis.

**Closed accounts.** A program charge is never billed on a closed service account.

### Questions answered by the rule

**May the service desk round or adjust an arrangement installment when it is billed?** No. The amount is taken verbatim from the arrangement record.

**Can a Budget Billing settle-up appear as a program charge line?** No. Budget Billing never produces a program charge.

superseded_clauses: Program charges count toward the past-due amount and the late charge like any other charge.
